question: How is birefringence of liquid crystal mixtures measured in the mid-infrared spectral range?
answer: Birefringence of liquid crystal mixtures in the mid-infrared (1900-5500 cm⁻¹) was determined using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy.  A test cell, consisting of germanium substrates with poly(vinyl alcohol) alignment layers and a known thickness, was filled with the liquid crystal.  This cell was placed between two wire grid polarizers within the FTIR spectrometer.  Transmitted intensity was measured at four analyzer angles (0°, 45°, 90°, and 135°) relative to a horizontally polarized input.  These intensities were then used to calculate the Stokes parameters and subsequently the birefringence.

### 1. **Summarize the purpose of the paper:**
The paper focuses on the development and characterization of a mid-infrared (MIR) intensity modulator based on a twisted nematic liquid crystal cell. The study involves measuring the Stokes parameters and birefringence of various liquid crystal mixtures in the MIR range (1900-5500 cm⁻¹) and demonstrates the use of germanium substrates as transparent electrodes. It also evaluates the performance of the modulator, which incorporates poly(vinyl alcohol) alignment layers and wire grid polarizers, achieving high contrast ratios.
